name: Breakable Walls
summary: Chop a hole through a wall, without paying thirty actors per wall for the destructibility nobody has used yet.
description: A rectangle cannot lose a piece, so the usual answer is to tile every wall up front and spend the frame budget on destruction that has not happened. Here a wall is one actor until something hits it, and only then becomes a grid of chunks with the hit ones removed -- lazily, with a hard ceiling on how many walls may be broken at once, because a mechanic with no upper bound degrades over twenty minutes in a way that looks like a memory leak. Every chunk keeps a collider, so the hole is real and the door stops being the only way in. Reads footprints from the collider rather than the sprite, which is what makes it safe in a world with height.
nextSteps: Put BreakableWalls.js on a manager actor and tag it Walls.
Tag destructible scenery Wall and give each one a BoxCollider2D.
Call damage(x, y, radius) from whatever swings or explodes; 0 back means a clean miss.
Set maxShattered from your frame budget, not from how generous it feels.
If the world has height, set chunkHeight and keep faceShade equal to Depth25D's.
